newsitem.title: USA: Fed eases firewalls between banks, securities firm. [CORRECTED 18:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Fed eases firewalls between banks, securities firm. [CORRECTED 18:35 GMT]

text.p: The Federal Reserve Board Wednesday eased three "firewalls" between banks and their securities affiliates.
The easing of the restrictions would allow employees of a bank to also work at the bank's "section 20" subsidiary.

However, the chief executive officer of a bank would still be prohibited from serving in that position at an affiliated section 20 subsidiary, and directors and officers of a bank would not be allowed to serve as a majority of the board of directors of the securities subsidiary.

The Fed also repealed "cross-marketing" (corrects from "cost-marketing") restrictions so that banks would be allowed to engage in marketing activities on behalf of the affiliated section 20 subsidiaries.
The third firewall that was loosened was related to restrictions on the purchase and sale of financial assets between a section 20 subsidiary and its affiliated bank.

Many government securities are already an exception to that restriction and the Fed expanded that exception to allow "assets having a readily identifiable and publicly available market quotation and purchased at that market quotation."
A section 20 affiliate is a separately capitalized subsidiary of a bank holding company that conducts securities activities not permitted in the bank.
